correctness.rationale: The homogeneous pinned Dirichlet recurrence on each cycle arc has the unique cosh solution, hence an arc is feasible iff its length is at most the established cutoff L. Removal of f original sources merges runs of at most f+1 original gaps; necessity also holds at k=f+1 with one survivor. Summing all k cyclic window inequalities gives (f+1)n<=kL. Balanced floor-difference gaps attain the bound with every (f+1)-window bounded by ceil((f+1)n/k), including all small and equality cases. Transfer-matrix trace counts the cyclic words; an n/k rooting double count gives labeled sets. Two standalone programs from this package replayed exact rational linear systems for 3,027 source sets, all admissible f<=3 and f=n-1 through n<=9, and 374 independent transfer comparisons, all PASS. Finite tests corroborate; the proof establishes the infinite domain.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper expressly identifies fault tolerance under source loss as a new direction; the claim resolves this natural model completely for all cycles, all real attenuation/floor parameters, and every admissible failure budget. It gives a sharp feasibility phase boundary, an exact worst-case placement cardinality, balanced explicit solutions, and a finite generating-function census of all optimal placements. Unlike a single computed small case or a no-failure corollary, it addresses the combinatorial coupling of arbitrarily many source losses and sharpness for an infinite family, which supports future placement and resilience comparisons.
